method.harness: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py run_instrumented via a narrow driver (prefill 1024 + N single-token forwards), profiled with rocprofv3 --kernel-trace
method.isolation: two traces (decode_steps=4 and 20) diffed per kernel; the 1024-token prefill cancels, leaving decode-only cost. The runs differ by 24 forwards (warmup + measured), which is the basis used below.
method.caveat: rocprofv3 inflates absolute kernel durations (~24% here); shares and rankings are the signal, absolute per-launch numbers come from the unprofiled microbenchmark.
method.jit: prebuilt outside the profiler, profiled run under HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 with a precomputed compiler-version file

per_decode_step.note: 1116 kernel launches per decode step (trace delta over 24 forwards). The 8.04 ms gap between summed kernel time and wall time is host dispatch/launch latency: 7.2 us per launch, not GPU work.

attention_kernel_microbench.run_to_run_spread_us: sliding keys=1024 measured 599-722 us across runs (clock state); rankings stable

hypotheses_closed.evidence: all-zero keep-mask (removes every K/V load, keeps the tile loop and reductions) is only 11% faster at sliding/1024 (497.9 vs 558.8 us) and 36% faster at full/1024 (756.8 vs 1184.7 us). Issued traffic runs at 46-81 GB/s, ~5-8% of the 960 GB/s peak, so bytes moved are not the limiter.

hypotheses_closed.hypothesis: decode attention is barrier-bound; a wider key batch per barrier round wins
hypotheses_closed.evidence: the launcher's tile selection was widened from a ceiling of 8 to 32 (the case 16/32 entry points were unreachable) and measured across the full curve at keys=1024, sliding: tile 1 = 817.3, 2 = 701.1, 4 = 633.6, 8 = 598.5, 16 = 1076.8, 32 = 722.5 us. tile=8 - the existing choice - is the optimum; four times fewer barrier rounds is slower, and register pressure from the wider per-thread slot/active arrays dominates. Change reverted; decode parity tests re-run green (37 passed).

mechanism.summary: the per-key cost (~0.5-0.6 us, ~1000+ cycles) is invariant to the work inside the key iteration: removing the mask load, the K load, the dot product, the 256-lane reduction tree, all four tile-loop barriers, the publish broadcast and the running-max chain each leaves the time within noise. The 256-thread / 8-warp / 5-barrier-per-8-keys structure is itself the cost.
mechanism.superseded_summary: latency-bound at very low occupancy with one dependent 2-byte load per thread per key (iteration 19) - not supported: removing those loads changes nothing on the sliding geometry.
mechanism.implication: micro-optimization inside the existing per-key loop cannot win; the lever is a different decomposition. Candidate: one warp per (token, head), 32 lanes x 8 dims, 16-byte vector loads, no shared-memory traffic and no barriers, with the 256-lane tree reproduced by 5 shuffle rounds plus 3 in-lane rounds in identical association order so the result stays bit-exact.
mechanism.constraint: any such change must keep the lane-to-dimension mapping, the ascending-j publish order, and the 256-lane tree, which tests/test_gpu_gemma4_attention_decode_parity.py enforces.

campaign_attribution_correction.previous: G3 pursued the MoE decode linears as the dominant decode cost, on iteration-15 trace figures of 9.15 ms/step (gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill_out) and 5.15 ms/step (q5_1_selected_gemv_bf16_bf16).
campaign_attribution_correction.current: those MoE kernels are 6.22 ms/step combined (13.6% of the token); decode attention alone is 24.03 ms/step (52.6%), and a further 8.0 ms/step is host dispatch across ~800 launches.
campaign_attribution_correction.consequence: the compact-MoE/Q5_1 line of work can move at most ~14% of the token; attention is the highest-value target by a wide margin.

corrections.reason: the zero-mask ablation was methodologically invalid; the NaN weight path left pass-3 V loads running

corrected_measurement.method: K and V loads replaced inside the tile/pass-3 bodies with load-free arithmetic, mask left valid, so the loop structure and every non-load instruction are preserved

corrections.consequence: the KV-bandwidth rejection stands but for the opposite reason: loads are ~0% of the sliding geometry and ~26% of the full geometry, so bytes moved are not the sliding limiter either
